holidays.name: National Bagel Day
holidays.description: A day for the chewy, shiny, hole-in-the-middle bread. Eat one plain, toasted, piled with cream cheese and lox, or turned into a breakfast sandwich.
holidays.origin: The bagel is tied to Jewish communities in Central Europe, and New York's bakeries made it a staple of American breakfast. This modern food holiday is an unofficial observance that bagel fans and brands now celebrate every January 15.
holidays.funFact: A real bagel is boiled briefly in water before it is baked. That step gives it the glossy crust and dense chew.

holidays.name: National Strawberry Ice Cream Day
holidays.description: A day for pink scoops in cones, cups and milkshakes, even though it's the middle of winter. Brain freeze is optional, but it tends to show up anyway.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It gives a classic parlor flavor its own moment in the freezer-aisle spotlight.
holidays.funFact: Botanically, strawberries aren't true berries. Their seeds sit on the outside of the fruit, and each one is technically its own tiny fruit.

holidays.name: National Hat Day
holidays.description: A day to wear your favorite headwear, from beanies and fedoras to top hats and baseball caps. In January it's also a good excuse to keep your ears warm.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular day for hat lovers to show off their toppers.
holidays.funFact: Hats have been worn for thousands of years. Some of the oldest known examples come from ancient Egypt and Bronze Age Europe.
